roadmap.title: The API Architect: Designing Robust Web Services
roadmap.description: Transition from ad-hoc data fetching to designing structured, scalable, and secure APIs. Master REST principles, HTTP semantics, data validation, and fundamental security practices to build web services that are robust and easy for other developers to consume.
roadmap.seniorInsight: A well-designed API is a contract with your consumers. If your API is inconsistent, poorly documented, or fails unpredictably, it will cause immense friction. Focus on clarity, predictability, and adhering to established standards over clever shortcuts.
prerequisites: Basic understanding of the HTTP Protocol (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE)
Proficiency in a backend language (e.g., Python, Node.js, Ruby)

branches.title: Phase 1: RESTful Principles & HTTP Semantics
branches.description: Understanding the foundation. Mastering resource-oriented design, proper use of HTTP methods, and status codes.

branches.title: Phase 2: Data Formatting & Validation
branches.description: Ensuring data integrity. Standardizing JSON responses, handling errors consistently, and validating incoming payloads.

branches.title: Phase 3: Pagination, Filtering, & Sorting
branches.description: Managing large datasets. Implementing strategies to efficiently retrieve and navigate through collections of resources.

branches.title: Phase 4: Fundamental API Security
branches.description: Protecting the endpoints. Understanding authentication (Tokens/API Keys), authorization basics, and common vulnerabilities.

steps.title: Resource-Oriented Design
steps.description: Structure your API around nouns, not verbs. Learn how to map business entities to URIs (e.g., `/users`, `/orders`) and avoid action-based endpoints (e.g., `/getUsers`).

steps.title: HTTP Methods: Idempotency & Safety
steps.description: Use the right tool for the job. Master the semantics of GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, and DELETE. Understand which methods are safe (read-only) and which are idempotent (repeatable without side effects).

steps.title: HTTP Status Codes in Practice
steps.description: Communicate effectively. Stop returning `200 OK` for errors. Learn when to use the 2xx (Success), 3xx (Redirection), 4xx (Client Error), and 5xx (Server Error) ranges appropriately.

steps.title: JSON Response Standardization
steps.description: Build predictable APIs. Design a consistent JSON envelope for all responses. Include metadata, data payloads, and structured error objects so clients always know what to expect.

steps.title: Input Validation & Sanitization
steps.description: Never trust the client. Implement robust validation on all incoming request bodies and query parameters. Return detailed `400 Bad Request` responses indicating exactly which fields failed validation.

steps.title: Offset vs. Cursor Pagination
steps.description: Handle growing lists gracefully. Understand the performance implications of `LIMIT/OFFSET` pagination (which degrades as datasets grow) versus the efficiency of Cursor-based pagination.

steps.title: Filtering and Sorting Semantics
steps.description: Give clients control over data. Design intuitive query parameter structures for filtering (e.g., `?status=active`) and sorting (e.g., `?sort=-createdAt`) collections of resources.

steps.title: Authentication: Tokens & API Keys
steps.description: Verify identity. Learn the basics of securing endpoints. Understand how API Keys are used for server-to-server communication and how JSON Web Tokens (JWTs) or Session Cookies manage user state.

steps.title: Authorization (RBAC Basics)
steps.description: Control access. Implement basic Role-Based Access Control (RBAC). Ensure that authenticated users only have permission to access resources they own or are authorized to view.

steps.title: Rate Limiting Concepts
steps.description: Protect against abuse. Understand the necessity of rate limiting to prevent Denial of Service (DoS) and brute-force attacks. Learn the basics of tracking requests per IP or user token.
